prompt: Over the first week in Jan 2025, in the Bluesky collection, what are the most prominent terms people are using, and which ones seem especially characteristic of that period?
ground_truth:
{
  "summary": "During the first week of January 2025, the most prominent terms in the Bluesky collection were a mixture of very high-frequency general discussion terms and politically focused terms. The strongest topical signals were around US politics, especially Trump, elections, presidency, government, democracy, Republicans/Democrats, law, media, and Elon Musk. The period also shows New Year and January-specific language, such as terms related to the new year, January, happiness, Christmas, and fireworks.",
  "key_points": [
    "The highest-frequency general terms included 'people' (64,583), 'year' (47,874), 'time' (42,216), 'thing' (30,709), 'day' (26,508), 'way' (25,868), and 'thank' (25,153).",
    "The most prominent topical term was 'trump' (47,883), indicating that Trump-related discussion was a major feature of Bluesky discourse during this week.",
    "Other strongly political terms included 'country' (17,466), 'president' (14,062), 'state' (12,423), 'maga' (11,271), 'election' (11,141), 'party' (10,530), 'government' (9,911), 'law' (8,982), 'Biden' (8,458), 'Republican' (8,183), 'Democracy' (7,594), and 'Democrat' (7,420).",
    "Terms such as 'Musk' (14,419), 'media' (12,747), 'Twitter' (4,601), 'platform' (3,496), 'Tesla' (3,469), and 'Elon' (8,013) suggest that platform politics, social media, and Elon Musk-related discussion were also especially visible.",
    "Terms characteristic of the specific period included 'new' (13,521), 'year' (47,874), 'January' (4,266), 'happy' (3,955), 'Christmas' (1,579), and 'firework' (1,148), reflecting New Year-related conversation alongside the political discussion.",
    "The returned terms are stemmed, so forms like 'presid', 'elect', 'govern', 'democraci', and 'januari' should be read as normalized versions of president/presidency, election/elect, government/governance, democracy, and January."
  ]
}
